section_summary: This section documents the dissemination, publication, and implementation of the Report of the United States Education Mission to Japan submitted to General Douglas MacArthur on March 30, 1946. It contains letters of appreciation from Mission members to Assistant Secretary of State William Benton, discussions on recruiting specialized educational advisers for SCAP, and requests from educational, religious, and civic organizations for copies of the report. The section also highlights widespread public outreach through speeches, NEA publications, and a gift collection of American children's books sent to Japanese schools.

subfiles.about: Acceptance of an invitation to meet informally with the Far Eastern Commission's education subcommittee in Washington.
subfiles.summary: Stoddard accepts an invitation to meet Dr. Sundaram and others at the Indian Agency on May 8.
subfiles.title: Telegram from George D. Stoddard to Frank A. Schuler, Jr. Regarding Far Eastern Commission Meeting

subfiles.about: Invitation to meet with Dr. M. S. Sundaram and the Far Eastern Commission's education subcommittee.
subfiles.summary: Schuler invites Stoddard to an informal gathering with Sundaram and subcommittee members on May 8.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank A. Schuler, Jr. to George D. Stoddard Extending Invitation to Far Eastern Commission Meeting

subfiles.about: Recommendation for the widest possible distribution of the Education Mission report.
subfiles.summary: Recommends wide distribution of the March 30 report, suggesting War Department funding if State Department funds are insufficient.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Frank A. Schuler, Jr. to E. R. Spaulding on Distribution and Printing of the Report

subfiles.about: Recommendation to release the U.S. Education Mission report to outside organizations.
subfiles.summary: Recommends that the March 30 report submitted to General MacArthur be distributed to interested external individuals and groups.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Henry P. Leverich to Francis Russell Recommending External Distribution of Report

subfiles.about: Recommended printing quantities and distribution lists for the Education Mission report.
subfiles.summary: Recommends printing 12,500 copies for Public Liaison distribution, noting Harold Benjamin's request for 5,000 copies.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from James E. Swihart to Francis Russell Regarding Printing and PL Distribution

subfiles.about: Noting minor textual errata in the Education Mission report and upcoming Washington schedule.
subfiles.summary: Stoddard lists typographical errata for correction and outlines his upcoming schedule in Washington.
subfiles.title: Letter from George D. Stoddard to Paul P. Stewart Noting Report Errata and Washington Travel

subfiles.about: Expression of appreciation for the privilege of serving as a member of the Education Mission.
subfiles.summary: Givens expresses gratitude for serving on the Mission, commends Stoddard's leadership, and offers further government service.
subfiles.title: Letter from Willard E. Givens to William Benton Expressing Appreciation for Service on Mission

subfiles.about: Reflections on the historic significance and unprecedented nature of the Education Mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Counts emphasizes that sending the Mission was historically unprecedented in relations between conqueror and conquered.
subfiles.title: Letter from George S. Counts to William Benton on the Historic Significance of the Education Mission

subfiles.about: Reflections on the Mission, emphasis on Japanese language reform, and commendation of Stoddard and Bowles.
subfiles.summary: Compton stresses that language reform is vital to Japan's future and encloses a copy of his letter praising MacArthur, Stoddard, and Bowles.
subfiles.title: Letter from Wilson Compton to William Benton, Enclosing Copy of Letter to Douglas MacArthur

subfiles.about: Appreciation for serving on the Mission and offering continued assistance with educational programs.
subfiles.summary: Benjamin expresses gratitude for serving under Stoddard and pledges Mission members' readiness to help further educational programs.
subfiles.title: Letter from Harold Benjamin to William Benton Regarding Follow-Up on Mission Report

subfiles.about: Gratitude for Mission participation and comments on favorable reception of the report in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Andrews expresses appreciation for his assignment and notes favorable comments on the Mission's report.
subfiles.title: Letter from John N. Andrews to William Benton on Reception of the Mission's Report

subfiles.about: Appreciation for serving on the Mission and hopes for democratic reorganization of Japanese education.
subfiles.summary: Diemer thanks Benton and hopes the recommendations aid in reorganizing Japanese education along democratic lines.
subfiles.title: Letter from G. W. Diemer to William Benton on Reorganizing Japanese Education

subfiles.about: Brief expression of gratitude for participation in the Education Mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Deferrari thanks Benton for his note and comments on the pleasure and benefit of participating in the Mission.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roy J. Deferrari to William Benton Expressing Thanks for Mission Participation

subfiles.about: Thanks for note and hopes for educational reconstruction in Japan and friendly bilateral relations.
subfiles.summary: Carnovsky hopes the Mission's work aids Japanese educational reconstruction and fosters friendly cooperative relations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Leon Carnovsky to William Benton on Educational Reconstruction in Japan

subfiles.about: Gratitude for participating in the Mission to Japan and contributing to the cause of peace.
subfiles.summary: Stoddard calls the trip a treasured experience and expresses gratitude for the opportunity to serve peace.
subfiles.title: Letter from Alexander J. Stoddard to William Benton on Participation in Education Mission

subfiles.about: Reflections on Mission participation and marveling at the coherency of the final report.
subfiles.summary: Horton thanks Benton for including her on the Mission and marvels at the report's coherence despite diverse opinions.
subfiles.title: Letter from Mildred McAfee Horton to William Benton on Coherency of Mission Report

subfiles.about: Personnel recommendations of candidate educators to serve as educational advisers in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Stevens recommends Floyd Reeves and Carleton Washburne as educational advisers, enclosing a letter from Louis V. Ledoux suggesting Dwight E. Minnich.
subfiles.title: Letter from David H. Stevens to William Benton, Enclosing Letter from Louis V. Ledoux on Educational Advisers

subfiles.about: Suggested reply to David Stevens detailing the educational adviser organization in SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Clarifies that Colonel Don Nugent holds the top educational post under General Ken Dyke and details eight specialized advisory positions being recruited.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from William T. Stone to William Benton Regarding Educational Adviser Positions in SCAP

subfiles.about: Clarification on specialized educational adviser openings in Japan and American Library Association shipments.
subfiles.summary: Benton clarifies that specialized advisers are needed under Nugent and discusses efforts to help the American Library Association deliver publications.
subfiles.title: Letter from William Benton to David H. Stevens Concerning Adviser Positions and Library Shipments

subfiles.about: Policy concerning private educational funds, Japanese domestic contributions, translations, and journals.
subfiles.summary: Discusses funding private Japanese institutions under MacArthur's purview, printed matter circulation, and scientific journal exchanges.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Frank A. Schuler, Jr. to Haldore Hanson on Educational Funds and Printed Matter

subfiles.about: Assessment of prospects for Japanese educational reform and recognition of progressive Japanese educators.
subfiles.summary: Freeman expresses optimism for reform if conditions remain stable for a decade, praising Japanese educators seeking change.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank N. Freeman to William Benton on Prospects for Educational Reform in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmission of NEA Leaders Letter No. 53 summarizing the findings and recommendations of the Education Mission.
subfiles.summary: Givens transmits Leaders Letter No. 53 distributed to 36,000 educators nationwide. The bulletin summarizes the Mission's background, contrasts Japanese authoritarian thought with democratic tenets, quotes Minister Abe, and outlines recommendations on curricula, Romaji language reform, decentralized school administration, teacher training, higher education, and adult education.
subfiles.title: Letter from Willard E. Givens to William Benton, Enclosing NEA Leaders Letter No. 53 on the Education Mission

subfiles.about: Transmission of NEA Leaders Letter No. 53 to Gordon T. Bowles on General MacArthur's staff.
subfiles.summary: Givens sends a copy of Leaders Letter No. 53 to Bowles in Tokyo, expressing appreciation for their cooperation in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Willard E. Givens to Gordon T. Bowles, Enclosing NEA Leaders Letter No. 53

subfiles.about: Request for copies of the Education Mission report for missionary Carl D. Kriete and committee members.
subfiles.summary: Requests an urgent copy of the report for Carl Kriete sailing from San Francisco and forty copies for the Japan Committee.
subfiles.title: Letter from Rowland M. Cross to Gordon T. Bowles Requesting Copies of Education Mission Report

subfiles.about: Response regarding copies of the Education Mission report sent to Dr. Kriete and the Foreign Missions Conference.
subfiles.summary: Confirms airmailing a copy to Dr. Kriete, encloses one copy, and notes GPO publication plans will enable bulk distribution.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank A. Schuler, Jr. to Rowland M. Cross Regarding Education Mission Report Distribution

subfiles.about: Request by Friends' General Conference for a copy of the Education Mission report.
subfiles.summary: Requests a copy of the March 30 report submitted to SCAP, offering to pay any required charges.
subfiles.title: Letter from Louis N. Grier, Jr. to Assistant Secretary of State Requesting Education Mission Report

subfiles.about: Transmission of the U.S. Education Mission report to Louis N. Grier, Jr.
subfiles.summary: Transmits an enclosed copy of the March 30, 1946 report submitted to the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank A. Schuler, Jr. to Louis N. Grier, Jr. Transmitting Education Mission Report

subfiles.about: Routing slip forwarding correspondence from E. B. Norton.
subfiles.summary: Routes an incoming letter from E. B. Norton (erroneously noted as 'Horton') for file.
subfiles.title: Reference Slip from J. Allen to Frank A. Schuler, Jr. Regarding Letter from E. B. Norton

subfiles.about: Report on public lectures and articles in Alabama regarding the Education Mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports addressing twenty civic and educational groups across Alabama and publishing articles in local periodicals.
subfiles.title: Letter from E. B. Norton to William Benton Reporting on Speaking Engagements in Alabama

subfiles.about: Gratitude for Mission participation and hopes for democratic educational reconstruction in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Wanamaker thanks Benton and hopes the report will help guide educational policy toward a peaceful and democratic Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Pearl A. Wanamaker to William Benton on Democratic Reconstruction in Japan

subfiles.about: Schedule of public lectures, college addresses, and radio broadcasts across Georgia and Tennessee.
subfiles.summary: Submits a list of extensive speaking engagements before educational, civic, and religious organizations and radio stations discussing Japan.
subfiles.title: Memorandum and Schedule from Emily Woodward on Public Speaking Engagements on the Japan Mission

subfiles.about: Commendation of Emily Woodward's extensive public outreach and speaking tour on Japan.
subfiles.summary: Schuler commends Woodward's extensive speaking engagements and outreach efforts regarding the Education Mission.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank A. Schuler, Jr. to Emily Woodward Commending Public Speaking Activities

subfiles.about: Inquiry and request for advice regarding impending appointment as civilian educational adviser in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Nichols reports he expects to serve as civilian adviser on educational reorganization under MacArthur and requests guidance.
subfiles.title: Letter from John R. Nichols to Frank A. Schuler, Jr. Regarding Appointment as Civilian Adviser

subfiles.about: Referral of prospective civilian adviser to the War Department Civil Affairs Division.
subfiles.summary: Speier refers Nichols to the War Department's Civil Affairs Division for informational pamphlets and field materials.
subfiles.title: Letter from Hans Speier to John R. Nichols Referring Inquiries to the War Department

subfiles.about: Request for advice based on Bowles's recent trip to Japan regarding adviser duties.
subfiles.summary: Nichols thanks Bowles for returning papers and requests suggestions regarding his prospective advisory role under MacArthur.
subfiles.title: Letter from John R. Nichols to Gordon T. Bowles Requesting Suggestions on Service in Japan

subfiles.about: Request from State University of Iowa Libraries for three copies of the Education Mission report.
subfiles.summary: Humphrey requests three copies of the March 30 report for the university library on the recommendation of C. H. McCloy.
subfiles.title: Letter from Mary Brown Humphrey to Gordon T. Bowles Requesting Copies of Report

subfiles.about: Transmission of one copy of the Education Mission report to the State University of Iowa.
subfiles.summary: Leverich sends one copy due to limited supplies, noting more copies will be available soon from the GPO.
subfiles.title: Letter from Henry P. Leverich to Mary Brown Humphrey Transmitting Copy of Report

subfiles.about: Inquiry on securing copies of the Education Mission report for dissemination in the United States.
subfiles.summary: DeForest asks how to obtain copies of the Mission's report to disseminate among friends of Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Charlotte B. DeForest to Gordon T. Bowles Inquiring After Education Mission Report

subfiles.about: Transmission of one copy of the Education Mission report to Charlotte B. DeForest.
subfiles.summary: Leverich sends one copy of the report, noting additional copies are expected soon from the Government Printing Office.
subfiles.title: Letter from Henry P. Leverich to Charlotte B. DeForest Transmitting Copy of Report

subfiles.about: Acknowledgment and thanks for copies of 'Education in Japan' and the Education Mission report.
subfiles.summary: Fahs acknowledges receipt of requested educational documents for the Missionary Research Library.
subfiles.title: Letter from Charles H. Fahs to Henry P. Leverich Acknowledging Receipt of Education Documents

subfiles.about: Graduate student request for the report of the Stoddard Committee on Education in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Sawyer requests a copy of the Stoddard report or inter-library loan information for graduate research on Japanese social studies.
subfiles.title: Letter from Michael O. Sawyer to Department of State Requesting Education Mission Report

subfiles.about: Report on the selection, purchase, and shipment of a gift collection of American children's books to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Carnovsky reports on the committee's work in spending $1,001.82 of donated funds to buy children's books through A. C. McClurg and Company. The books, sent with a custom bookplate and film, were turned over via SCAP CIE to the Japanese Ministry of Education to rotate among schools. Includes an eight-page classified bibliography of selected titles across picture books, classics, folklore, religion, arts, literature, science, and nature.
subfiles.title: Report by Leon Carnovsky to Members of the U.S. Education Mission on Children's Book Gift to Japan, with Bookplate and Booklist
subfiles.to: Members of the U.S. Education Mission to Japan
